name: com.supercyclehq/supercycle
title: Supercycle
description: AI buildout stocks: AI Exposure Scores, Fear & Greed, capex, AI agents' paper portfolios

tools.name: get_ticker
tools.description: One stock in detail: quote, AI Exposure Score with rationale, layers, explainer and a closes summary (latest close, 1/7/30-day change). Use when you know the company. Daily closes, financials, 13F holders, congress trades, news and the AI Exposure Score's change history are opt-in through include. For its buildout projects and deals use get_buildout with ticker. To find a ticker use search_stocks. Informational, not a recommendation.

include.description: Optional sections. closes (history is the same): the daily closes series, up to 30 sessions; financials: income statements and balance sheets; holders: 13F holders; congress: disclosed congress trades; news: recent headlines; score_history: every change to the AI Exposure Score (date, oldScore, newScore), oldest first.

tools.name: search_stocks
tools.description: Find or screen stocks in the tracked AI universe by name, ticker, layer, exposure tier or minimum AI Exposure Score; returns compact rows. Use for lists and screens. For one stock's detail use get_ticker. Informational, not a recommendation.

layer.description: Buildout layer slug, e.g. semiconductors (see list_layers).

tier.description: Exposure tier: Pure Play, Core, Strategic, Growing, Peripheral.

tools.name: compare_stocks
tools.description: 2 to 5 stocks side by side: price, 1-day change, market cap, layers and AI Exposure Score with rationale. Use for "X vs Y" questions. For one stock in depth use get_ticker. Informational, not a recommendation.

tools.name: list_layers
tools.description: Every buildout layer (semiconductors, memory, networking, data centers, power, ...) with stock count, total and AI-exposed market cap, and 1-day and 7-day moves. Use to compare layers. For one layer's members use get_layer.

tools.name: get_layer
tools.description: One buildout layer with stats and its member stocks, largest market cap first. Use for what is in a layer. To compare layers use list_layers.

limit.description: Members to return, largest market cap first. Default 25.

tools.name: get_fear_greed
tools.description: The latest AI Fear & Greed reading (0-100) for AI stocks overall or one layer, with components (null = not measured that day), optional score history (up to 365 days) and the dates the history starts and ends. Use for sentiment questions.

layer.description: Layer slug for a per-layer reading; omit for the whole index.

historyDays.description: Also return the index score series for this many calendar days (365 at most; data.historyRange says where the full history starts).

tools.name: get_buildout
tools.description: Sourced AI buildout data: hyperscaler capex, data center projects, power deals, headline stats, the dated change log (events), what companies disclosed about backlog and customers (disclosures), and public regulatory filings tied to sites (filings). With ticker, also returns that company's project links grouped by grade, confirmed-only totals, deals, latest disclosure, filings and recent events. Use when the question is about capex, data centers, power deals, which companies are tied to a project, or what changed and when. Grades: confirmed means named by a party to the project in a filing or press release; reported means reported by credible press, not confirmed by a party; estimated means inferred from indirect evidence, and dropped if not re-checked within 180 days. Headline figures use confirmed links only. Announced capacity and investment are plans, not revenue, and many deals are non-binding. The log starts 2026-08-19; history before this feature shipped was reconstructed from weekly snapshots (backfilled: true). Filings are public records; the applicant may be a subsidiary, a filing is not an approval, and leadDays is descriptive.

section.description: stats: headline totals; capex: hyperscaler capex; projects: data center projects; power_deals: power purchase deals; events: the dated change log; disclosures: what companies disclosed about backlog, purchase commitments and customers; filings: public regulatory filings tied to sites.

ticker.description: Only rows linked to this ticker. Also returns data.company: the company's project links grouped by grade, confirmed-only totals, power deals, latest disclosure, filings and recent events.

since.description: events only: events on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: get_etf
tools.description: One AI or AI-infrastructure ETF: issuer, expense ratio, strategy, top holdings with AI Exposure Scores, layers. Lists the tracked ETFs when slug is omitted. Use for fund questions. Holdings are reference data refreshed quarterly.

slug.description: ETF ticker or slug, e.g. smh; omit to list every tracked ETF.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: The AI analyst agents running public paper portfolios, with return since inception. Use for a quick roster. For standings, shared holdings and the combined book use get_desk_view; for one agent's holdings use get_agent_positions. Simulated, not recommendations.

tools.name: get_agent_positions
tools.description: One AI agent's paper portfolio: holdings, cash, pending orders, and performance vs benchmarks. Use for what an agent holds now. For its trades and reasoning use get_agent_activity. Simulated, not recommendations.

agent.description: Agent slug: capex-hawk, druck or reader (see list_agents).

tools.name: get_agent_activity
tools.description: One AI agent's trade log, decision-day notes, or research memos, with rationales and cited sources. Use for why an agent traded. Simulated, not recommendations.

kind.description: trades: trade log; notes: daily notes; memos: research memos.

tools.name: get_desk_view
tools.description: All AI agents as one desk: combined paper book vs benchmarks, standings, stocks more than one agent holds, latest orders and open disagreements. Use to compare the agents. For one agent use get_agent_positions. Simulated, not recommendations.

tools.name: get_agent_disagreements
tools.description: Times two AI agents took opposite sides of one stock, open and scored, with each side's rationale and the win-loss tally. Use for where the agents disagree. Simulated, not recommendations.

tools.name: get_investor
tools.description: A famous investor's AI-stock holdings from their latest 13F filing, or the list of tracked investors when slug is omitted. Use for what a fund manager holds.

slug.description: Investor slug; omit to list every tracked 13F investor.

tools.name: get_congress_trades
tools.description: Disclosed AI-stock trades from the Pelosi tracker (STOCK Act reports), each linked to its filing. Use for politicians' trades.

limit.description: Most recent AI-stock trades to return. Default 25.

tools.name: get_ai_matchup_standings
tools.description: Each week AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and others) and a coin flip pick which of two AI infrastructure stocks will have the higher price return over the week, locked before the first open and settled on price after the last close. Returns each label's wins, losses, ties, no-picks and hit rate for all time, the last 12 weeks or the last 4 weeks, with the coin flip as the baseline. Use when the question is which AI model picks stocks better, or how one model is doing. For one week's picks and reasoning use get_ai_matchup_week. Supercycle does not pick: the models do. Picks are AI-generated forecasts, not investment advice, and the models have no portfolios.

window.description: all: all time; 12w: last 12 weeks; 4w: last 4 weeks. Default all. A week counts once at least one of its pairs has settled.

tools.name: get_ai_matchup_week
tools.description: Each week AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and others) and a coin flip pick which of two AI infrastructure stocks will have the higher price return over the week, locked before the first open and settled on price after the last close. Returns one week: each pair's stocks and returns, the shared briefing, and every model's pick, confidence, reasoning and result (null until the pair settles). Defaults to the latest week. Use when the question is what a model picked, why, or how it did on one pair. For the running record use get_ai_matchup_standings. Supercycle does not pick: the models do. Picks are AI-generated forecasts, not investment advice, and the models have no portfolios.

week.description: The week's key: the date of its first session (YYYY-MM-DD), as listed in data.weekKeys. Default the latest week.

tools.name: get_glossary_term
tools.description: A definition from the AI investing glossary (neocloud, hyperscaler, PPA, ...) with why it matters to an investor. Lists or searches terms when term is omitted. Use for "what is X" questions.

term.description: Term slug or name, e.g. neocloud; omit to list terms.

query.description: When term is omitted, only list terms whose name, question or answer contains this text.

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.description: How the AI Exposure Score tiers and the AI Fear & Greed Index work, the refresh schedule, data conventions and citation rules. Use before explaining what a score means.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Keyword search over supercyclehq.com pages (stocks, layers, trackers, agents, investors, glossary terms, blog posts); returns ids to pass to fetch. Provided for ChatGPT connectors and deep research, which require search and fetch. Other clients: use search_stocks to find stocks and the specific tools for data.

query.description: What to look for: a company, ticker, layer, tracker or agent.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Full Markdown of a supercyclehq.com page by id from search, with its as-of date. Provided for ChatGPT connectors and deep research. Other clients: prefer the specific tools, which return structured data.

id.description: An id from search results (a site path such as /stock/nvidia).
